summary.summary: PARTIAL extending the pinned-set solve to a LINE of sources: c = M^-1 alpha with M the Green matrix solves the pinned problem exactly for n = 2, 3, 4 collinear sources - every pinning condition holds and (I - P) m vanishes at every unpinned site - and the solve shows what a pair cannot: at n = 3 the charges are [0.528563241, 0.447653871, 0.528563241], symmetric end-to-end with the INTERIOR source carrying strictly less charge than the ends because it is screened on both sides, while n = 4 wraps this L = 4 torus into a closed ring on which all four charges are equal, there being no ends; the total charge grows with the line while the charge PER SOURCE falls, from 0.692647018 for an isolated source to 0.439033578 at n = 4, so a longer line, and a fortiori a closed ring, is cheaper per site to hold at the same pinned value (exact on a 4x4x4 torus, 7-point stencil, killing 1/10)

review: Took the item my own a3 (issue 8543) named: M^-1 for a line of sources. The solve holds for n = 2,3,4 collinear - pinning conditions and (I-P)m = 0 at every unpinned site - and shows two things a pair cannot: the charge is position-dependent, with the interior source at n = 3 carrying strictly less than the ends because it is screened on both sides, and the charge per source falls monotonically with the line's length, so a longer line is cheaper per site to hold. The run also caught a finite-size feature I had not anticipated: at n = 4 on an L = 4 torus the line wraps into a closed ring, all four charges become equal because every source is translation-equivalent, and there are no ends - so that row is the ring case, not a longer line. I relabelled it rather than dropping it. That leaves only n = 2,3 as genuine lines, two points, which is why the trend is stated as numbers rather than as a law. Every number in the summary is interpolated from the computation.
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 5: Two persistent sources under light-cone formation: the interaction, done dynamically. GIVEN (refereed): linear light-cone formation has static response chi = 7/E(k) (the lattice Green function) and equal-time covariance C = 7 sigma^2/(2E(1 - E/14)), with chi/C = (1 + phi)/sigma^2 (the naive fluctuation-response relation fails by the factor 1 + phi); the Coulomb coefficient of C is 7 sigma^2/(8 pi r). Referee's correction to two failed attempts: a source PINNED AT EVERY LEVEL is not a conditioning of the stationary Gaussian at one time; the pinned process has stationary mean alpha G(y)/G(0) with G = (I - P)^-1. Executed (simulator probes/lib/formation_response.py): the nonlinear sphere law's potential around a persistent field source is 0.96-0.99 of (h/beta) x the lattice Green function, symmetric. TASK: (a) for the linear process with two sites pinned at every level to values a and b at distance r, compute the stationary law's cost: the large-deviation rate per level (the probability that the unpinned process stays within the pins), as a function of r; its sign for like and unlike pins; the coefficient of 1/r; (b) the same for two FIELD sources h_1, h_2 (no pinning): the change of the stationary mean and of the rate; is there an 'interaction energy' at all for a non-equilibrium process, and what replaces it (the rate function, or -log pi for the reversible law: compute both and compare); (c) superposition at linear order and the first nonlinear correction in 1/beta. Verify on L = 6..16 tori exactly. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/persistent-sources/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route.
